items.title: George "Happy" Schilling Interview, 1957-09-08
items.q: Little Paul in Detroit told me he was in town about a year ago. He told me that Bakay died and he was telling me about his sons and made good musicians.

ctx.x: From the Chicago movement? That's right. That's right.

Right there. And the other thing was jaffy. We didn't know what jazz was down here. We went there. We called ourselves a ragtime band. To the rock around there, they called them the Nick LaRocca and jazz band. But before they first worked, there was the Dixieland band. They added the name jazz to it. They worked at the Shilla Cafe at a while. Of course you knew, some guy in New York made them a big oven and went to the Palais Royal. There ain't no more Palais Royal in New York now, but that's where they went…
It's only one up there. It's only one.
